findings.title: Bit-exact parity claim conflicts with acknowledged neighbor-order divergence
findings.description: The architecture document (100-arch.behavior-engine.md:34) makes tick determinism a core principle. The slice's unit-test plan compares neighbor output "as sets" because "order within a row may differ for grid" (Testing Strategy), yet Implementation Notes step 5 requires "bit-exact position equality against brute-force-only over N ticks" in the integration test. CSR-native force evaluation (slice 111) sums per-row via `np.add.reduceat`; a different neighbor order changes floating-point summation order, so bit-exact parity across a mid-run backend switch is not guaranteed by anything in the design. The design should state explicitly whether cross-backend FP-order divergence exists and, if so, replace the "bit-exact" criterion with an appropriate tolerance — otherwise the integration test is specified to fail for reasons that are not a dispatcher bug.

findings.title: `initial_backend` is documented as operator-selectable but absent from the config surface
findings.description: The "Brute as Initial Backend" decision says the initial backend is made configurable "so an operator running a scattered-start scenario can choose grid-first," and the class signature exposes `initial_backend`. But `SpatialConfig` defines only `backend`, `grid_threshold_mean_neighbors`, and `hysteresis_band` — there is no YAML field for the initial backend, and no validation rule for it. Either add the field to `SpatialConfig` or remove the claim that operators can choose it; as written, the design promises a knob the specified config surface does not deliver. (The hardcoded `"brute"` in `_build_spatial` also contradicts the "no magic defaults" project convention unless it is surfaced at the config level.)
